newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT says capex likely to rise in next few years.
newsitem.headline: NTT says capex likely to rise in next few years.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp president Junichiro Miyazu said on Wednesday that the firm's capital investment is likely to increase in the next few years due to investment in China and other parts of Asia as well as in new services.

"We will increase investment in international projects, especially in China and other Asian countries and by doing so may boost our overall capital investment in the next few years," Miyazu told Reuters in an interview.

NTT currently makes capital investment of about two trillion yen a year, mainly on domestic infrastructure. Decisions on restructuring had led to speculation that NTT may cut this heavy investment to increase profits.
Miyazu said NTT would enter a new era of focusing on profit and shareholder-orientated management and move away from heavy investment in domestic infrastructure.
He also said that the company plans to announce in June next year profit forecasts for after its restructuring, which is due to be completed in June 1999.
Asked if NTT was considering inviting outside directors to join the company, Miyazu said: "We have no plans for the time being."
However, he added that the firm would invite outside directors in the future. Asked whether this would happen at the time of the restructuring, he replied: "That would be well after restructuring."
Miyazu denied speculation that NTT might merge its loss-making Personal Handyphone unit, NTT Personal, with its cellular phone unit NTT DoCoMo at the time of the restructuring.
